system.name: HDBO survey and benchmark (poli, poli-baselines)
system.one_liner: A survey of high-dimensional Bayesian optimization methods for discrete sequences, with a benchmark of standardized black-box functions.

content.variant_note: a radial genealogy: one large disc whose radius is the publication year (2012 at the centre, 2024 at the rim) and whose sectors are method families, with white lineage arrows between method pills
content.argues: High-dimensional Bayesian optimization methods fall into seven families plus a remainder, and their lineage since 2012 can be read from one radial timeline.
content.subject: about 100 method pills placed by year and by family on a blue disc, with arrows between methods that build on each other

content.reading_order: Starts at the centre (2012) and moves outwards along the rings; the eye then follows the sector colours and the white lineage arrows, with sector names read along the rim.

layout.arrangement_note: One big circle fills the figure; eight angular sectors, 13 concentric rings and pills in each sector; sector names run along the outer rim, the year labels along the vertical axis and the one-line OSS key sits at the lower right outside the disc.

palette.used_for: outer rings of the disc (latest years)
OSS badges and the OSS key

style.stroke: no stroked shapes; thin black ring lines and sector spokes are drawn as filled hairlines, white arrows are the only visible line work
style.font: sans (embedded Type 3) 5.5 pt for method names, 6-6.5 pt for year labels, 2 pt for OSS badges; sector names set along the rim
style.arrows: thin white curved arrows with small heads, many crossing
style.effects: soft drop shadows under the pills

encoding.color_means: pill colour = method family (green non-linear embeddings, yellow linear embeddings, crimson trust regions, lavender additive models, teal variable selection, olive gradient information, salmon structured spaces, mauve other); blue shade of the rings = time band, darker for newer
encoding.line_style_means: white curved arrow = one method explicitly augments or uses another; thin black circle = year; straight spokes = sector boundaries
encoding.shape_means: pill = one method; grey tag = open-source implementation; disc = the whole field
encoding.marker_means: OSS badge = open-source implementation; year numbers on the vertical axis label the rings
encoding.emphasis: family colours are the strongest signal; white arrows stand out against the dark blue
reusable_patterns: radial timeline: radius = year (oldest at the centre), angle = family, each method a pill at its year radius inside its family sector
white curved lineage arrows between pills

new_tags.name: radial-genealogy

lessons.what_to_learn: Encode time and family in one picture: radius is the year, sector and pill colour are the family, and arrows give who builds on whom; pin a tiny badge to the pills that carry a property of interest and explain it in a one-glyph key.
lessons.suits: surveys of a method family where chronology, categories and lineage must be read together and the number of items is large.

evidence: A timeline of high-dimensional Bayesian optimization methods, with arrows drawn between methods that explicitly augment or use each other.

methods are grouped according to their most dominant feature

summary: The survey maps high-dimensional Bayesian optimization methods for discrete sequences on one radial timeline. A large blue disc has 13 concentric rings, from 2012 at the centre to 2024 at the rim, and eight angular sectors for the method families: non-linear and linear embeddings, trust regions, additive models, variable selection, gradient information, structured spaces and other. Each of about 100 methods is a pill coloured by family and placed at the radius of its year; tiny OSS badges mark open-source code; white curved arrows join methods that explicitly augment or use each other; a one-line key explains the badge.
